title: Programming basics check
instructions: Answer all four questions. You need 70 to pass, and you can retry as often as you like.

questions.prompt: What does a computer do with the instructions in a program?
options: Guesses the intent behind vague ones
Rewrites them to be more efficient
questions.explanation: A computer does exactly what the instructions say, in order. Vague or wrong instructions produce wrong results.

questions.prompt: In the largest-number algorithm, what do you do with the first number?
options: Remember it as the biggest seen so far
Add it to the last number
questions.explanation: You start by remembering the first number as the biggest so far, then compare every other number against it.

questions.prompt: Which statement about algorithms and coding is correct?
options: The steps are the algorithm; translating them into a language is coding
Typing is the algorithm; the steps are coding
questions.explanation: The thinking (the steps) comes first. Coding is the translation of those steps into a language.

questions.prompt: Following the algorithm on [3, 9, 4], what is the biggest-so-far after looking at 4?
questions.explanation: It starts at 3, becomes 9 when 9 is seen, and stays 9 because 4 is not bigger.

title: Order the steps
instructions: Put the steps of the largest-number algorithm in the correct order using the arrow buttons.
lines: Remember the first number as the biggest so far
If it is bigger, remember it instead
When the numbers run out, report the one you remembered
